BLOCKED: three lowering defects stop the move, so nothing was committed. Report: /home/user/Nikaia/docs/briefs/k3a2-comptime-compute.md.report.md

All the preconditions are on `develop`. The run-3 patch applied cleanly, and after #1012 the lowered trait takes `&impl Fn`, as intended. `lower-std` runs clean, but the lowered Rust does not compile:

1. **`Sync` name clash.** A `let`-bound lambda with a declared type (`not_here`) lowers to `Kept<dyn Fn(..) + Send + Sync>`. Inside `tools`, `Sync` resolves to the `pub enum Sync` in `ty.nika`, and rustc stops with E0404. The emitter should write `std::marker::Sync`.
2. **Missing `&`.** The untyped inner `known` lambda has the same name as the parameter it reads. When it is passed to the recursive call it is written `known`, not `&known` (E0308). Without that shadowing, the same form gets its `&`.
3. **Endless recursion at instantiation.** A recursive function whose `fn` parameter lowers as `&impl Fn`, and which passes itself a new lambda, never stops instantiating. A 15-line `nikaia run` probe gives "Reached the recursion limit while instantiating `deep::<{closure}>`". The Rust being moved uses `&dyn Fn` for exactly this reason. `comptime_computed` and `comptime_worked_out_ahead` need that form.

The brief says a lowering defect stops the slice and is not worked around, so I made no edits outside its files. To check how far the code got, I edited the generated file by hand as a probe (fixing 1 and 2): `cargo check` then passed. Defect 3 would only show up when `nikaia` is built, and the probe above confirms it. I then put all my files back by name.

The next run can start from `docs/briefs/k3a2-comptime-compute.run4.patch` (untracked; `git apply --check` passes). It is the run-3 patch with the inner `known` lambda left untyped, so #997's change types it from the call it is passed to.

The report says `Needs:` a fix of defects 1–3. Disk: 3.7 GB free, test cache 4.0 GB, no new cache entries over 100 MB.
